summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with a history of end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, and diabetes was admitted for acute shortness of breath due to pulmonary edema from fluid overload and tachycardia. She had incomplete fluid removal during her prior dialysis session, leading to volume overload. She was treated with emergent hemodialysis, which removed 1.7 liters of fluid and improved her respiratory status. Her heart rate was controlled by switching to verapamil and reducing metoprolol to prevent hypotension. A urine culture showed Klebsiella, and she was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone followed by oral cefpodoxime. Her warfarin was continued at home dose despite a subtherapeutic INR, as bridging was deemed unnecessary. She was discharged home with nursing services, new medication instructions, fluid and sodium restrictions, and plans for extended weekend dialysis to prevent recurrence.
